name: Engraving
overview: Scripture reveals the significance of engraving as a means of consecration and identity, particularly in the context of the priesthood and Israel's relationship with God. The names of the twelve tribes were carefully engraved on onyx stones set in the high priest's breastplate and girdle, symbolizing God's covenant and remembrance of His people (Exodus 28:9, 21; 39:6, 8). Additionally, the priest's crown bore the engraved inscription "HOLINESS TO THE LORD," emphasizing the sacred dedication required for service (Exodus 28:36). However, engraving was also used in idolatry, as seen when the golden calf was fashioned with a graving tool, highlighting the contrast between holy use and profane misuse (Exodus 32:4).
